lots.guide_summary: All 16 surviving entries are SOLD Gowans hammers (premium extra), AUD, no conversion. There are no UNSOLD or ASKING entries. Seven weighed sterling chains of 21-44g made $55-$110 (median about $80). Lighter sterling chains and mixed pendant and earring lots made $10-$70. Plain dress jewellery lots made about $22. None of these is the same item, and our chain is not described or confirmed as sterling.
lots.working: No maximum bid yet because the curb chain's metal is unconfirmed: the catalogue says only '3 NECKLACES & EARRINGS', no mark can be read, and every SOLD entry is a close or category comparable, not the same item. Only if a 925 mark is confirmed and the chain weighs 25g or more: lowest close SOLD = $55 (25g, Gowans lot 412857), so keep = 55 / 1.22 = 45.08, rounded down to $45 hammer ($54.90 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $80 hammer at Gowans, less about 20% selling fees and $0 postage (sold locally) = $64, then 64 / 2.44 = 26.2, rounded down to $25. Not worth flipping. Melt check: 30g sterling = 27.75g fine x A$2.69/g (silver A$83.68/ozt, gold-api.com 2026-10-16, 1 USD = 1.446 AUD) = about $75, so a confirmed 30g sterling chain sits at about melt. If the chain is plated or stainless the lot is worth about $20.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read (single 450x600 photo), the metal is unconfirmed, the catalogue does not say sterling, and there is no same-item SOLD. Comparables are close weighed sterling chains whose pages were opened.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped outright. Corrected bid counts for lots 393273 and 394888, and the date and bid mix-up on the $20/$12 entry. Moved the 13-17g chains from 'close' to 'category guide' because they weigh about half what our curb chain probably does. Added five weighed 21-44g sterling chains and one pendant and stud set from the same Gowans search. Armitage past results not checked: WebSearch budget used up.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged the clasp area. Lobster clasp with flat end tags. Grey tarnish in the links suggests silver rather than stainless steel, but no 925 or other stamp is legible. lots.question_for_armitage: Is the curb chain stamped 925 or sterling (usually on the clasp or end tag), and what does it weigh? Are the pendants and studs marked 925?

lots.guide_summary: All 10 surviving entries are SOLD Gowans hammers, AUD, premium extra. All are category guides, none the same item. Single older half crowns made $30-$70. Small mixed British coin lots made $20-$55. One 8-coin silver lot made $190 (upper bound). No UNSOLD or ASKING entries. Melt floor (not a sale): about $85-$90 of silver in the four silver coins.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD, so no maximum bid. Melt floor (silver A$83.68/ozt = A$2.69/g fine, gold-api.com 2026-10-16, 1 USD = 1.446 AUD): 1880 half crown 14.14g x .925 = 13.08g fine = about $35 (less for wear); 1921 and 1929 half crowns 14.14g x .500 = 7.07g each = about $19 each, $38 together; NZ coin .500 = $15 (florin) to $19 (half crown). Silver total about $88-$92, so call it $80-$90 allowing for wear. Ten worn pennies add about $5-$15. Dealers usually pay 80-90% of melt, so at the viewing a sensible ceiling is about $65 hammer ($79.30 all-in). This is guidance only, not a SOLD-based maximum.
lots.confidence_reason: Dates read from the flips and the NZ legend read in an enlarged crop, but there is no same-item SOLD; every comparable is a category guide (pages opened). The melt figure is a floor, not a sale.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher's two range entries ('$20-$35, 3 lots' and the 'about 100 penny lots, $20-$110' summary) are not single sales. The first is split into three verified single lots; the second is dropped as a SOLD entry because it is a summary of many lots, not one priced sale. Corrected the identification of the fourth coin: it is New Zealand ('GEORGE V KING EMPEROR'), not Australian. Armitage past results not checked: WebSearch budget used up.
lots.key_photo_findings: Flips are hand-labelled 'Half Crown 1880 GB', '1929 GB VF' and '1921 GB VF'. The 1880 Victoria head is worn almost smooth (about Good to VG). The 1921 looks the best (about VF). The loose coin reads 'GEORGE V KING EMPEROR' with a crowned, robed bust, so it is a New Zealand 1933-36 type. Pennies show Britannia reverses with dates 1889(?), 1902(?) and 1910 readable. Several have green verdigris spots and dark patina.
lots.condition: Circulated. Silver coins are Good to VF. The pennies are worn (Fair to Fine) and some have corrosion spots.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the date and denomination of the loose New Zealand coin (half crown or florin)? Are there exactly four silver coins? Are there any coins on the other side or beneath that the photo does not show?

lots.guide_summary: All 12 surviving entries are SOLD Gowans hammers, AUD, premium extra, and all are category guides for single components or mixed silver lots. Single marcasite animal brooches made $35-$60. Single sterling thimbles made $55-$100. Mixed sterling charm and jewellery lots made $35-$100. No same-item, UNSOLD or ASKING entries. The lot's value mostly depends on total sterling weight, which is unknown.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD, so no maximum bid. The pieces look like modern figural sterling (the catalogue says 'including sterling silver pendants'), and the bear, hand clips, figure and whistle look fairly solid. Melt if sterling: A$83.68/ozt x .925 / 31.1035 = A$2.49/g (gold-api.com 2026-10-16, 1 USD = 1.446 AUD). At 60g that is about $150; at 100g about $250. Category SOLD results for the separate pieces add up to well over $150 if they are all marked. Ask for the total weight and marks before bidding. Rule of thumb at the viewing: stay under about 70% of sterling melt on the weighed marked pieces, as hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: No hallmarks legible in the single photo, weight unknown, possible mix of sterling, continental silver and plate. Only category-guide SOLD entries, with pages opened.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all researcher entries re-found in the Gowans API. Split the researcher's combined thimble, charm and citrine entries into single verified lots, and corrected the bid count on lot 425829 (6, not 4). Dropped the vague 'QTY OF COLLECTABLES INCL STERLING SILVER $180' and 'QTY OF ASST JEWELLERY INCL SILVER $330' mentions as guides, because their contents are unknown. Hand clips show cuffed hands holding fans with textured plaques. The bear is large (about the height of the box) and well modelled. The whistle has a feather pattern and a ring end. The rings have a yellow oval stone and a red square stone, possibly citrine and garnet or glass. No marks are legible at this resolution.
